hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3), acting through disrupted lipid metabolism (cholesterol, lipid droplets, sphingolipids)
B: late endosome / lysosome function (degradation, acidification, cholesterol egress, autophagic flux, lysosomal enzyme activity)
scope: IN: late endosome/lysosome function (cholesterol or lipid accumulation in lysosomes, NPC1, lysosomal degradation, cathepsin activity, lysosomal pH, autophagic flux, LAMP1 compartments) measured in APOE4 vs APOE3 cells, especially where linked to lipid/cholesterol metabolism; manipulations of lipid metabolism that change late-endosome/lysosome function in APOE4 cells. OUT: lipid changes with no late-endosome/lysosome readout, mitochondrial respiration alone, inflammation or transcriptomics alone.
